Flag the draws of a csfmt_ensemble_v4 above a historical limit

Source: R/v4_hlm.R
signal_detection_hlm_v4.Rd

Compares every draw of measure with the historical limit, the 99.5% quantile of a normal fitted to the same weeks in earlier years. The method is that of signal_detection_hlm() for a csfmt_ensemble_v3, and the values are identical.

Usage

signal_detection_hlm_v4(x, measure, baseline_isoyears = 5)

Arguments

x

The csfmt_ensemble_v4, full or compressed.

measure

The name of the draw matrix to compare with the limit. It MUST NOT end in a reserved suffix.

baseline_isoyears

The number of earlier years in the baseline.

Value

x with the new draw matrix <measure>_hlm, which holds 1 for null, 2 for high and NA with no limit, with a levels attribute. It adds these columns to $data:

  • <measure>_hlm_thr: the limit.

  • <measure>_hlm_prob_null and <measure>_hlm_prob_high: the share of the draws at each level, which is NA when every draw is NA.

The shares give every ordinal percentile of the level codes, so the step writes no percentile column.

Each new name MUST be at most 63 bytes. A rerun on the same measure replaces the draw matrix and the columns. The input x does not change.

Details

The baseline of a week uses the median of the draws of each earlier week. It holds the medians 52, 104, and so on up to 52 * baseline_isoyears rows back in the same series, each with its two neighbours. The limit is qnorm(0.995, mean, sd) of those values. A week that lacks any of them, or has an NA in them, gets no limit. A year back is 52 rows, so across a 53-week ISO year the baseline is one week off.

A draw at or above the limit is high, and otherwise null. A draw with no limit, or an NA draw, gets NA. The share of draws at a level describes the nowcast uncertainty. It is not a p-value, a posterior probability or a false-alarm rate.

The function draws no random numbers. The function takes no ..., so a misspelt argument is an error.

See also

Other v4 functions: as_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_reporting_triangle_v4(), ens_add_rate_v4(), ens_compress_v4(), mem_thresholds_v4(), nowcast_ecdf_v4(), nowcast_passthrough_v4(), print.csfmt_ensemble_v4(), short_term_trend_v4()

Examples

w <- cstime::dates_by_isoyearweek$isoyearweek
iyw <- w[match("2017-01", w) + 0:319]
set.seed(1)
ens <- csfmt_ensemble_v4(
  data.table::data.table(location_code = "nation", isoyearweek = iyw),
  id_cols = "location_code",
  draws = list(cases = matrix(rpois(320 * 100, 50), nrow = 320))
)
ens <- signal_detection_hlm_v4(ens, measure = "cases")
tail(ens$data[, .(isoyearweek, cases_hlm_thr, cases_hlm_prob_high)], 3)
#>    isoyearweek cases_hlm_thr cases_hlm_prob_high
#>         <char>         <num>               <num>
#> 1:     2023-05      52.76397                0.37
#> 2:     2023-06      52.56387                0.30
#> 3:     2023-07      52.38206                0.33
